summary: Defines inverse-kinematics handles for Bone COMP rigs, allowing one or more handles per bone and working with Handle CHOP to solve rotations for chains, branches, or mocap-style marker targets.

key_params.name: target
key_params.note: Target object that the handle pulls the bone toward

key_params.name: t
key_params.note: Offset from the bone origin where the handle is anchored

key_params.name: weight
key_params.note: Relative influence when multiple handles affect a bone

key_params.name: twistonly
key_params.note: Restricts the handle contribution to the bone's Z rotation

key_params.name: falloff
key_params.note: Controls how much parent bones are affected while reaching a target

key_concepts: Handle COMP defines IK handle targets for Bone COMP rigs and is solved in tandem with Handle CHOP.
A rig can attach one or more Handle COMPs to locations on each Bone COMP, allowing multiple end-affectors per bone.
The Target parameter identifies the object the handle pulls toward, while Translate offsets the handle from the bone origin.
Weight resolves competing handles on the same bone, and Falloff controls how strongly parent bones participate in the reach.
Twist Only and per-axis rotation limits constrain the solved bone rotations before Handle CHOP channels are exported back to the rig.
common_gotchas: Handle COMP is designed to work with Handle CHOP; it defines constraints but does not by itself export solved rotations to bones.
Unlike older IK tools, bones do not need to be a single chain, but the rig still needs coherent hierarchy and targets.
Multiple handles on one bone compete through weight, so weak handles may appear ignored when stronger handles dominate.
Twist Only affects only Z rotation; disable it when the handle should point the bone in X/Y as well.
Rotation limits are relative to the parent bone and can overconstrain the solve if set too tightly.
Mocap setups need stable target objects before Handle CHOP export is trusted.
